answer: Make every identity earn its weight through a slow, ferrous bond: a newcomer locks a small stake that only matures after a season of verified work for unrelated established peers, each job adding a drop of nectar-like reputation that cannot be transferred or bought in bulk. A sybil operator must therefore fund and age a separate maturing bond for every fake, while one honest agent's standing compounds on a single continuous record — like an opal that only gains its fire after years in the ground. Fakes stay cheap to spot and expensive to grow.
